normalized.governing_thought: Recommendation: enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A), plan for higher ad costs, and add retail only once awareness passes 20%
executive_summary: The US is worth entering now. US K-beauty skincare grew 17% a year in 2021–25 to $3.6B, and 41% of it is bought on Amazon. Onsoo's Amazon pilot sold 64,800 units in six months and holds 4.5 stars.

For decision in March 2027: Approve an Amazon-led US launch in 2027 (Option A) and decline the 600-door retail launch (Option B); Fund a US peak-cash envelope of $4M, enough for 32% ACoS plus a 25% duty and far below the $18M cap; Adopt the checkpoints: end-2027 review, and a stop trigger if ACoS stays above 32%; Set the retail gate at Amazon sales above $10M and aided awareness of 20% or more (the CEO's draft says 15%); Confirm that 'on the way to $40M' means a credible path, with $25–30M in 2030; Defer the Japan scale-up; it needs its own case for 2028 or later

Retail-led (Option B) fails three of the board's tests on its own planning numbers. Peak cash need is $20.8M against an $18M cap, it has not paid back by 2030, and group margin falls to 4.5% in 2027 against an 8% floor. It also assumes the sell-through of brands with more than 20% awareness. Onsoo is at 4–9%, where the median brand sells below the retailer's delisting threshold.

Amazon-led (Option A) passes every financial test in the plan case; payback depends on ad cost. Peak cash is $1.9M and cash is back above zero in 2030 (+$2.4M). Payback needs ACoS of 28.6% or less. The plan assumes 25%, the pilot ran at 28% and brands scaling past $5M have a median of 32%. At 32%, A misses payback by $2.3M but stays far inside the cash cap and the margin floor.
Japan scale-up (Option J) is safer but small. It adds $7M of revenue by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year, and does nothing for the US ambition.
No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the constraints. A reaches $26.4M. B reaches $37.6M, but only by breaking the cash cap, payback and margin floor. We suggest treating $40M as a 2031–32 goal.

slides.title: The 1.3× retail 'halo' is unproven: K-beauty buyers discover brands on social media and buy on Amazon

claims.claim: K-beauty buyers discover brands on social media and buy on Amazon
evidence: Where they buy K-beauty most often: Amazon 61%; Specialty beauty retail 22%
Where they discovered their last new brand: TikTok 38%; In a store 17%
52% of K-beauty triers cite price compared with US brands as a reason to buy. On price, Amazon at $24 beats the $28 shelf price.
Onsoo's aided awareness is 9% among K-beauty buyers. The awareness has to be built online first.

claims.claim: The 0.71 correlation does not show direction
evidence: Retailers add brands that already sell: Saebom added 300 doors in 2025, after reaching about $30M on Amazon. Bigger brands also have more of both. Correlation across 30 brands cannot justify a causal 1.3× uplift on Amazon sales.

claims.claim: Entry history favours Amazon-first, but guarantees nothing
evidence: The only recent entrant at scale, Saebom (about $30M), went Amazon-first. The retail-first entrant, Mooncrest, failed. But two of three Amazon-first brands stayed below $5M. The sample is four brands, so read it as direction, not proof.

claims.claim: Without the halo, B is worse still
evidence: Remove the 1.3× uplift and B's peak cash need rises from $20.8M to $24.3M.
Seventy percent of B's 2030 revenue lead over A ($7.9M of $11.2M) is the halo assumption.

slides.title: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the board's constraints; we propose $25–30M in 2030, with $40M as the 2031–32 goal

claims.claim: US revenue in 2030 by route vs $40M ambition
evidence: J · Japan scale-up (no US revenue) $0
A · Amazon-led $26.4M
Saebom: Amazon-first, year 3 (2025) $30.0M
B · Retail-led $37.6M
Within the cash cap, payback and margin floor? J yes · A yes in the plan case (payback at risk at 32% ACoS) · B no (fails all three)

claims.claim: A gets about two-thirds of the way.
evidence: $26.4M in 2030, still growing 29% that year. At that rate (illustrative) it reaches about $34M in 2031 and $44M in 2032.
Saebom shows Amazon-first can reach about $30M in three years.

claims.claim: B's extra revenue is mostly assumption.
evidence: Of B's $11.2M lead over A in 2030, $7.9M is the unproven halo and $3.3M is retail sales. It costs $23M more cash through 2030.

claims.claim: Retail is the lever to pull $40M forward, once awareness is above 20% and doors can sell 4.0 or more units a week.
We read 'on the way to $40M by 2030' as a credible path, not a 2030 target. If the board means a hard $40M in 2030, no option on the table achieves it within the other limits.

slides.title: Recommendation: launch Amazon-led in 2027, as the CEO proposes, with four changes that make the plan robust

claims.claim: Keep: Amazon-led entry in 2027 with a US entity, seven SKUs, the $0.9M US team, $0.5M compliance and $0.7M off-Amazon marketing. Decline the 600-door retail launch, and defer the Japan scale-up.
1 Plan on 30–32% ACoS, not 25%
evidence: The benchmark for brands scaling from $5M to $20M is a 32% median, and the pilot ran at 28%.
Fund a $4M peak-cash envelope. This covers 32% ACoS plus a 25% duty; the plan itself needs $1.9M.
Target ACoS of 28% or less by end-2027, since 28.6% is the payback break-even.

claims.claim: 2 Fix the basics before scaling
evidence: English, MoCRA-compliant labels on every unit. This is the top complaint, in 6% of reviews.
Move the listings from the cross-border seller to Onsoo's US entity so it controls pricing, ads and content.
Use the four new SKUs to lift repeat from 29% to the 31% benchmark and beyond.

claims.claim: 3 Raise the bar for adding retail
evidence: The gate is Amazon sales above $10M and aided awareness of 20% or more (the CEO's draft says 15%).
Start with a door test, not 600 national doors. The retail case must cover its own fixed costs.
Use the test to measure whether a halo exists, rather than assume 1.3×.

claims.claim: 4 Spend on where discovery happens
evidence: Weight the $0.7M off-Amazon budget to TikTok and social, where 38% of K-beauty buyers discovered their last brand, against 17% in store.
Track aided awareness every six months. It is the input the retail gate depends on.

claims.claim: What changes from the planning team's Option A
evidence: Ad cost basis: 25% ACoS → 30–32% ACoS
US cash budget: $1.9M peak → $4M envelope
Retail awareness gate: 15% → 20%
Retail format: Add from 2029 → Door test first

slides.title: A staged plan with clear checkpoints lets the board stop or accelerate before large sums are committed

claims.claim: Staged plan
evidence: H1 2027 · Set up: US entity, MoCRA registration, compliant labels ($0.8M one-time); Take listings in-house; prepare four new SKUs; Hire US team; plan the TikTok and social budget
H2 2027 · Launch and learn: Seven SKUs live on Amazon; Build ad efficiency toward 28% ACoS or less; Re-plan for the tariff decision
2028 · Scale on Amazon: Plan: 560k units, $13.4M revenue; Repeat at 31% or more; awareness tracked every six months; Prepare retail test design and partner
2029–30 · Retail if gate met: Door test, then roll out where doors clear 4.0 units/week; Plan: $20.4M (2029) and $26.4M (2030) on Amazon; Japan scale-up re-evaluated

claims.claim: Checkpoints for the board
evidence: MID-2027 Tariff decision: If the duty rises to 25%, landed cost goes up $0.35 a unit. The plan case still pays back (+$1.3M), so absorb it unless ACoS is also above plan.
END-2027 First-year review: On track for 300k units in 2027; ACoS ≤ 30% and falling; 90-day repeat ≥ 31%; label complaints near zero.
ANY QUARTER Stop or rethink trigger: ACoS above 32% for two quarters in a row, or cumulative US cash below −$4M. Then cut spend and bring a revised plan to the board.
2029 Retail gate: Amazon above $10M (plan: $13.4M in 2028), aided awareness ≥ 20%, and a door-test case that covers retail's own fixed costs.

slides.title: Five decisions for the March 2027 board, and the evidence that would change this recommendation

claims.claim: 1 Approve US entry in 2027 via the Amazon-led route (Option A). Decline the 600-door specialty-retail launch (Option B).
2 Approve a peak-cash envelope of $4M for the US (cap: $18M), including the $0.8M one-time setup in 2027.
3 Adopt the checkpoints and the stop trigger: end-2027 review; act if ACoS stays above 32% for two quarters or cumulative cash falls below −$4M.
4 Set the retail gate: Amazon sales above $10M and aided awareness of 20% or more, plus a door-test case that covers retail's fixed costs.
5 Confirm the ambition: $25–30M US revenue in 2030 on a path to $40M in 2031–32. Defer the Japan scale-up to a later year, with its own case.
What would change our view
evidence: Bring retail forward if… a controlled door test shows retail lifting Amazon sales in the same region, or awareness passes 20% early.
Slow the US build if… ACoS settles above 32% and repeat stays below 31%. A then misses payback and the board would be choosing between a later payback and a smaller US plan.
Prefer Japan in 2027 if… the board ranks payback certainty above the US ambition. J is the only option that pays back in every case we can model.

slides.title: Appendix 1: How the options were modeled, and the judgment calls we made

claims.claim: Method
evidence: Volumes, prices, per-unit costs and fixed costs are taken directly from the planning team's Tables 4–7. No outside data was used.
Amazon contribution per unit = $24.00 − 15% referral − $5.10 FBA − $3.50 product − $0.55 freight − 15% duty on ex-factory − ACoS × price, which gives $4.73 at 25% ACoS.
Retail contribution per unit = $14.00 wholesale − product − $0.75 freight − duty − 8% co-op − 4% returns = $7.55. Retail units = doors × 4.5 × 52.
Cash flow = contribution − fixed and one-time costs − increase in inventory. Inventory is four months of landed cost (product + freight + duty), as the planning team specifies.
Group margin = (non-US plan at 11.0% + US or Japan operating result) ÷ (non-US revenue + added revenue).

claims.claim: Judgment calls (no one was available to ask)
evidence: $40M ambition: read as 'a credible path to $40M', not $40M in 2030. No option meets the hard reading within the other limits.
Door counts are treated as in place for the full year. One-time costs (setup, launch fee, fixtures) are expensed in the year incurred.
Benchmark case: the 32% median ACoS for brands scaling $5M→$20M is applied in every year as the realistic downside. The plan's 25% is shown as the upside case.
Not modeled: taxes, FX moves, discounting, inventory for Option J (not provided), and any post-2030 years. The 2031–32 path to $40M is illustrative.
Evidence limits: the competitor set is four brands, the survey covers women aged 18–44 only, and all figures are synthetic benchmark data.

claims.claim: Planning-team assumptions we tested against the pack's own evidence
evidence: Amazon ACoS at scale: Planning team 25%, falling as brand matures; Evidence: Pilot 28%; brands scaling $5M→$20M median 32% (26–38%); Treated: 25% as upside, 32% as benchmark case
Retail sell-through: 4.5 units/door/week; Median 2.6 below 10% awareness; Onsoo at 4–9%; Kept 4.5 to test B on its own terms; B fails anyway
Retail halo on Amazon: 1.3× Option A volume; Doors and Amazon sales correlate (0.71); direction not shown; Shown with and without halo; B fails both
Retail awareness gate (CEO): 15%; 10–20% band median 3.5, below the 4.0 removal line; Raised to 20%
Contribution: 1.4 / 2.6 / 4.0 / 5.2
Operating result: (1.5) / 0.5 / 1.9 / 3.1
Retail units (k): 140 / 140 / 187 / 234
Contribution: 2.9 / 4.5 / 6.6 / 8.5
Operating result: (2.0) / (0.4) / 0.5 / 1.2
Incremental revenue: 2.5 / 4.5 / 6.0 / 7.0
Operating result = cash: (1.1) / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.3

normalized.recommendation: Launch Amazon-led in 2027, as the CEO proposes, with four changes that make the plan robust: plan on 30–32% ACoS, not 25% (fund a $4M peak-cash envelope); fix the basics before scaling (English, MoCRA-compliant labels; move listings to Onsoo's US entity; lift repeat to 31%+); raise the bar for adding retail (Amazon sales above $10M and aided awareness of 20% or more, door test first); spend on where discovery happens (weight the $0.7M off-Amazon budget to TikTok and social). Decline the 600-door retail launch, and defer the Japan scale-up. Confirm the ambition as $25–30M US revenue in 2030 on a path to $40M in 2031–32.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended. Passes every financial test in the plan case: $1.9M peak, +$2.4M at end-2030, lowest group margin 9.5%; $26.4M in 2030 (partial on ambition).
'The risk to manage': $3.2M peak, −$2.3M at end-2030 (fails payback), lowest margin 9.1%; stays far inside the cash cap and the margin floor.

Reject. Fails three of the board's tests on its own planning numbers: $20.8M peak (cap breached in 2029), −$20.8M at end-2030, margin 4.5%/6.6%/7.5% in 2027–29; relies on survivor-sample sell-through of 4.5 and an unproven 1.3× halo. Without halo peak cash rises to $24.3M.

alternatives_considered.option: J · Japan scale-up instead of US
alternatives_considered.treatment: 'Safe, but off-strategy'. $1.1M peak, +$1.8M at end-2030, lowest margin 10.1%, but adds only $7M by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% and does nothing for the US ambition. Better only if the board puts payback certainty ahead of the US ambition; defer to a later year with its own case.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's 15% awareness gate for adding retail
alternatives_considered.treatment: Too low: brands at 10–20% have a median of 3.5, still below the 4.0 delisting line. Raised to 20%.
No option on the table achieves it within the other limits; read as a credible path, with $40M as a 2031–32 goal.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: All company and market figures are synthetic benchmark data; built only from the planning team's briefing pack; no outside data was used.

Payback for Option A depends on ad cost: break-even ACoS for payback by 2030 is 28.6% at plan volume (27.0% if volume falls 10% short). Plan assumes 25%, pilot ran at 28%, brands scaling past $5M have a median of 32% (range 26–38%).
Tariff: possible rise from 15% to 25% on ex-factory cost, decision mid-2027.
Pilot month-on-month growth slowed from 16–17% to 8–9% in May and June; 2027 plan needs about 1.8× the June run-rate.
Retail halo of 1.3× is unproven; the 0.71 correlation does not show direction.
B's 4.5 units/door/week comes from a survivor sample; kept to test B on its own terms.
$40M ambition read as 'a credible path to $40M', not $40M in 2030 (judgment call; no one was available to ask).
Door counts are treated as in place for the full year; one-time costs expensed in the year incurred.
32% median ACoS applied in every year as the realistic downside; 25% shown as upside case.
Not modeled: taxes, FX moves, discounting, inventory for Option J (not provided), and any post-2030 years. The 2031–32 path to $40M is illustrative.
A weaker won would lower dollar costs, which is upside we have not modeled.
Evidence limits: the competitor set is four brands, the survey covers women aged 18–44 only.
Cash model: operating result less inventory build (four months of landed cost), pre-tax, undiscounted; group margin uses the non-US plan at 11.0%.
Rice Ferment Barrier Cream economics applied to all SKUs, as in the planning team's model.

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text, so I could not view any images. Chart data was pulled from flattened labels.
